question.problem: Suppose that $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-t$ represents the position of a race car along a straight track, measured in feet from the starting line at $t$ seconds. What is the average rate of change of $s(t)$ from $t=1$ to $t=3?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-t$ be the position of the race car in feet after t seconds. To find the average rate of change of $s(t)$ from $t=1$ to $t=3,$ we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[1,3]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δs}{Δt} & =\frac{s(b)-s(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{s(3)-s(1)}{3-1} \\  & =\frac{[2(3)^{3}-(3)]-[2(1)^{3}-(1)]}{2} \\  & =\frac{51-1}{2} \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average rate of change of $s(t)$ is $25$ feet per second.
